subject: Sample Syntax for Second Order Multivariate Growth Curve with Covariates

messages.author: fd3e215f916e6052
messages.subject: Sample Syntax for Second Order Multivariate Growth Curve with Covariates
parts:
Hello Awesome Lavaan Group!

I'm starting my dissertation analysis and am having trouble finding sample syntax for a more complex multivariate (i.e., parallel process) and second-order growth curve model. 

My aim is to assess the impact of a host of predictors, both time-varying and time-invariant, on two growth trajectories that are modeled from second-order DVs at each time point. I have found many separate resources on how to model second-order growth curves, multivariate growth curves, and adding a single time-invariant or single time-varying covariate. Many questions arise when thinking about putting all of these different aspects together and expanding the number of covariates into a single model. I was hoping someone may have attempted a similar project successfully and would not mind sharing their code. 

I really appreciate any and all help! Also, please let me know if this is not an appropriate question form for this google group as I have not used it before.

messages.author: edceb8dce9472a62
messages.subject: Re: Sample Syntax for Second Order Multivariate Growth Curve with Covariates
parts:
Hello, 

Covariates:
You can include predictors which are time-variant by regressing the manifest variables directly onto them. if you have multiple covariates, simply keep adding them to the regression. 

 manifest1_wave1 ~ covariate1_wave1 + covariate2_wave1 + ...
 manifest1_wave2 ~ covariate1_wave2+ covariate2_wave2 + ...

OR
 
intercept ~ covariate1 + covariate2 +...
slope ~ covariate1 + covariate2 +...

etc. 

Time invariant predictors can be controlled for by putting them on the manifest or latent variables (though choice of which will change df and the model to some extent). It will "eat up" a lot of df to put them on the manifest variables, but some research questions will be better answered in this way. 

Second-order curves & PPMs
The parallel process model (PPM) can be extended to second order, but depending on your research question this may or may not be ideal. You only capture whatever is common among those variables and will lose variance in each construct every time you group more things together. 

That being said, you'll be able to modify/extend this: 

model <-
'
## first order, putting together multiple constructs at each wave
constructA_wave1 =~ manifest1_wave1 + manifest2_wave1 + manifest3_wave1
constructB_wave1 =~ manifest4_wave1 + manifest5_wave1 + manifest6_wave1
constructC_wave1 =~ manifest7_wave1 + manifest8_wave1 + manifest9_wave1

constructA_wave2 =~ manifest1_wave2 + manifest2_wave2 + manifest3_wave2
constructB_wave2 =~ manifest4_wave2+ manifest5_wave2 + manifest6_wave2
constructC_wave2 =~ manifest7_wave2 + manifest8_wave2 + manifest9_wave2

etc. for more constructs/waves

##second order 
wave1 =~ constructA_wave1 + constructB_wave1 + constructC_wave1
wave2 =~ constructA_wave2 + constructB_wave2 + constructC_wave2

 etc. for more waves

##Growth 
Intercept =~ 1*wave1 + 1*wave2 + ... etc.
Slope =~ 0*wave1 + 1*wave2 + ... etc. 
'

Keep in mind there are important specification rules for SEM & even more stringent ones for multilevel SEM. 

I do not believe you will be able to test goodness of fit with only 2 waves of data, as I presented here. To see what you'll need, you can draw a path diagram and assess the number of df you have.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: Sample Syntax for Second Order Multivariate Growth Curve with Covariates
parts:
Hi Chris,

Wow, thank you very much for the clear and modifiable syntax. I do have some additional questions if you do not mind.

1. Can you confirm that I am supposed to regress the manifest variable onto each covariate instead of the latent DV I create? I think I did not use the correct language in my first post and I am not doing second-order, instead, I meant to say that I am keeping my DV at each wave latent (sorry for your extra work, but I do appreciate it!). So, one of my DVs in the parallel process will be positive self-perceptions of aging (PSPA) which is made from 4 items. Could I control for time-varying covariates like:

PSPA_wave1=~manifest1_w1 + manifest 2_w1 + manifest3_w1 + manifest4_w1 

PSPA_wave1=~covariate_1 + covariate_2

or do I have to regress each manifest onto the covariates as you wrote?

2. With my general understanding rounding out, where can I find more information about the specification rules? 

2a. For instance, I believe I'll need to correlate all the covariates, both time-invariant and time-varying? 

A little bit more specifics about my project in case it helps direct anyone's response: my plan is to model PSPA and negative perceptions of aging (NSPA) for my parallel process across 4-times points. I will start with the same set of covariates mapped onto each growth trajectory and then remove non-significant covariates to find the optimal developmental model. Any info on specifying the relationship between covariates for one process and across the two processes would be extremely helpful!

Thank you, Chris, and anyone else who chips in. It is great to have some support and a community to discuss these topics with. I'll be sure to post a generalized syntax once my project is done to guide future researchers.

messages.author: edceb8dce9472a62
messages.subject: Re: Sample Syntax for Second Order Multivariate Growth Curve with Covariates
parts:
1. You can regress growth terms onto covariates OR wave by wave onto the manifest. I'm not sure if anyone has done a simulation comparing these, but ideologically the difference is what variance you are partialing out (in latent or manifest variables, respectively). See this resource for syntax on doing time variant vs. invariant (https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/growth.html).

You are basically just going to take the code form here and use it two times (changing labels for the second construct) to go from a latent growth curve to a parallel process model.

re: the code you sent, Notice the `=~` operator is for measurement model (i.e., making the latent) and `~` is the regression.

2. Google: SEM specification rules, and look for pages like this (one of the first links: https://psu-psychology.github.io/psy-597-SEM/07_full_sem/full_sem_specification.html), but if you're doing a PPM that isn't second-order, you will be fine with 4 waves of data for two constructs and some exogenous covariates (up to and including quadratic models, I believe, but definitely linear).

2a. The correlation of the covariates occurs by default (as it would with multiple regression, too), but you could write it out if you wanted. 

One more thing: Some people will not be a fan of this post-hoc removal of covariates, but some people are okay with it. Just report it if you do it. 

"Any info on specifying the relationship between covariates for one process and across the two processes would be extremely helpful!" If I am understanding you correctly (correlations of covariates predicting 1 latent growth curve that is not predicting the other), this is all specified automatically. Without changing defaults which should only be changed with good reason, you do not need to specify anything.
